subject: BenchSpec agreement & SLO runbook (post-discovery)
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: BenchSpec agreement & SLO runbook (post-discovery)

Tom — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the benchmark scope and avoid churn on measurement definitions.

Key customer SLOs you emphasized:
- P95 generation latency <= 250ms for short completions (<= 64 tokens)
- Sustained throughput target: 250 reqs/sec for peak hour
- Concurrent sessions target: 120 concurrent streaming sessions with incremental token streaming
- Streaming constraints: per-chunk latency <= 80ms (chunk = 32 token windows)

What Redwood will deliver for the benchmark run:
1) Prompt set (attached: edgespec_prompt_set_v1.json) — 1.2k prompts across short/medium/long tails and streaming-friendly turns.
2) Measurement definitions doc (draft) — enumerates metrics, warm-up, sampling, and rejection rules (we'll attach a formal version after your feedback).
3) Eval harness repo and run instructions (we'll provide a hosted runner and Docker image for reproducibility).
4) One benchmark window (3 hours) where we reproduce steady-state and spike scenarios.

Open questions / decisions needed from your side:
- Confirm the GPU family you'd like the run to reflect (A10G, A100, or T4-equivalent). We can provide results for two hardware points if helpful.
- Do you want quantized model variants included in the same run, or should we run them separately?
- Access: we'll need a short-lived VPN key or a signed scan-account service account to hit your staging endpoint for real-world ingress.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- You confirm the hardware target and access method by EOD Wed (16 Jun).
- We'll update the measurement doc and send a final BenchSpec (DocuSign link) for signature.
- Schedule benchmark window for week of 22 Jun (approx 3-hour window + 2-hour analysis).

Attachments: edgespec_prompt_set_v1.json (prompt samples + tags)

Thanks — looking forward to locking this down.

— Mina

Subject: Re: BenchSpec agreement & SLO runbook (post-discovery)

Mina — appreciate the thorough summary. A few clarifications before we sign off: 

1) Hardware: target A100 for the primary run (matches our production profile). If you can also provide a T4-like run for cost comparison, that'd be ideal but not required for acceptance.

2) Streaming: when you say "per-chunk latency <= 80ms", do you measure end-to-end (generator -> client) or server-side generation only? We need server-side numbers for SLAs; end-to-end will vary with client pipeline.

3) Reproducibility: we need a short checklist that explicitly calls out: random seed handling, KV cache persistence between warm-up and measurement, exact model config (quantization bits, operator kernels), and whether tokenization differences are normalized. Can you send that as a small checklist we can circulate to our infra team?

4) Access: we can create a staging service account and open a source CIDR for the benchmark runner. Who should I send credentials to? Is it safe to send to an SRE distribution list (sre@edgecommerce.com)?

If you can answer 2 and 3 in this thread, we'll fast-track approval. We're targetting the week after next for the window, so timing is tight.

— Tom

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: BenchSpec agreement & SLO runbook (post-discovery)

Tom — great questions. I've pulled a concise measurement contract (attached) and a proposed runbook below. Please review; this is what we'll execute against unless you request changes.

Attachment: benchspec_measurement_definitions.docx — includes acceptance criteria and gating rules.

Summary of our measurement contract (server-side focused):
- Metric definitions: P50/P90/P95/P99 generation latency (server-side time from request received by container to last token produced by model). Streaming per-chunk latency measured at model emit time.
- Warm-up: 15 minutes of mixed traffic, same prompt distribution, to populate caches and stabilize kernels. Sampling begins after warm-up.
- Run phases: 1) Baseline ramp (30m), 2) Sustained load (60m) — target throughput 250 rps, 3) Spike test (10m bursts at 700 rps with 60s recovery), 4) Graceful scaling test (simulate autoscale events).
- Reproducibility checklist (short):
  * Fixed tokenizer and vocab hash; tokenizer version captured in run metadata.
  * Model artifact SHA + quantization config recorded.
  * Seed: set RNG seed for sampling ops where applicable, record seed.
  * KV cache handling: cold start + persistent hot-cache sequences; we will run a deterministic cache-warm phase.
  * Operator kernel log: collect kernel selection trace (for later triage).

Acceptance gating for pass/fail (proposal):
- P95 <= 250ms for short completions AND no more than 2% of requests returning 5xx or timeouts during sustained phase.
- Streaming per-chunk median <= 60ms during streaming phase.

Operational asks for EdgeCommerce:
- Provide staging service account to sre@edgecommerce.com and the CIDR we should use for benchmark runners.
- Confirm whether recording of raw request/responses is permitted (we can mask tokens if needed) — required for some quality regressions.

If that looks good I'll stitch this into the formal BenchSpec doc and Mina will kick the DocuSign for the run authorization.

— Marissa

Thanks Marissa — that contract is exactly what our ops team needs. Quick answers: 

- Server-side measurement is what we'll base SLAs on — good to confirm.
- We'll provide the staging service account to sre@edgecommerce.com today; expect the key via secure transfer.
- Recording: OK to record request/response for the benchmark if Redwood applies token masking. We'll also sign the short data handling addendum.

We can commit to hardware: A100 primary, please include a T4-cost-comparison appendix if it's low-lift for you.

Availability: Friday 26 Jun or Tue 30 Jun both work for the 3-hour window. Which do you prefer?

Also, please send the finalized BenchSpec via DocuSign and a shared Drive link for the prompt set. I'll route to legal/ops once that's in.

— Tom
